column1: # Profile routes: the names both languages agree on and what `bench run`
# starts for each wrapped request. Read by the Rust tests (runner.rs) and the
# Tab-separated. '#' starts a comment line. A '-' field is empty. In a route,
# <dir> is the folder the wrap writes into (<output-dir>/<binary>.<canonical
# tool>) and <bin> the benchmark; arguments are separated by single spaces.
# escape   <--profile>  <--profile-output-dir>  <output option>  <its value in the route>
# %q{VAR} and %% in the value and refuse any other '%': each '%' of the
# folder is doubled; the output lands in the folder as named)
# unwrapped   <--profile>  (the benchmark runs itself; --profile-args reach it untouched)
